key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants require coordinated geometry, surface architecture, and biomaterial design to balance cyclic load support with durable bone integration.
engineering_relevance: Implant and coating design must jointly manage bending, shear, micromotion, and interface durability under realistic gait loading.
method: Systematic review of implant biomechanics, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation.
Synthesis of gait-phase finite element analysis, geometry optimization, and graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures.
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies.
evidence_signal: More than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level, with animal and human studies providing a smaller validation layer.
watch_item: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite concepts rely predominantly on non-DWBI analog studies and need device-specific fatigue, coating-integrity, and biological validation.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
